Write the sum to infinity for each geometric progression:
$$S_{\infty, 1} = \frac{3a}{1 - r}$$
$$S_{\infty, 2} = \frac{a}{1 - (-2r)} = \frac{a}{1 + 2r}$$

Equate the two sums and cancel $a$ ($a \ne 0$):
$$\frac{3a}{1 - r} = \frac{a}{1 + 2r} \implies 3(1 + 2r) = 1 - r$$

Solve the linear equation for $r$:
$$3 + 6r = 1 - r \implies 7r = -2 \implies r = -\frac{2}{7}$$

Set up the sum of the first $n$ terms for the first arithmetic progression ($a_1 = 15, d_1 = 19 - 15 = 4$):
$$S_{n, 1} = \frac{n}{2}\left(2(15) + (n - 1)4\right) = \frac{n}{2}(30 + 4n - 4) = \frac{n}{2}(4n + 26) = 2n^2 + 13n$$

Set up the sum for the second arithmetic progression ($a_2 = 420, d_2 = 415 - 420 = -5$):
$$S_{n, 2} = \frac{n}{2}\left(2(420) + (n - 1)(-5)\right) = \frac{n}{2}(840 - 5n + 5) = \frac{n}{2}(845 - 5n)$$

Equate the two sums and solve for $n$ ($n \ne 0$):
$$2n^2 + 13n = \frac{n}{2}(845 - 5n) \implies 4n + 26 = 845 - 5n$$
$$9n = 845 - 26 = 819 \implies n = \frac{819}{9} = 91$$
